title: Income statement & discontinued operations — Brightline Corp.
instructions: Brightline Corp. is finalizing its Year 2 statement of income and comprehensive income. Use the trial balance extract and the memo to compute the required amounts, then review the draft disclosure for errors. Tax rate: **25%** on all items.

exhibits.title: Pretax amounts, Year 2
exhibits.content:
| Item | Amount |
|---|---:|
| Net sales | 2,400,000 |
| Cost of goods sold | 1,440,000 |
| Selling, general & administrative | 520,000 |
| Interest expense | 40,000 |
| Loss from hurricane damage (unusual) | 60,000 |
| Outdoor Division: operating loss for Year 2 | 90,000 |
| Outdoor Division: loss on sale | 110,000 |
| Unrealized gain on AFS debt securities (pretax) | 16,000 |

*Revenues and expenses of the Outdoor Division are **excluded** from the lines above except for its two separately listed items.*

exhibits.title: Memo from the CFO
exhibits.content: In October we sold our entire Outdoor Division to exit the recreational products market, which represented about 25% of revenue. Its operations and cash flows were tracked separately. The hurricane loss was the first in the company's 40-year history.

rows.label: Income from continuing operations before income taxes
rows.explanation: 440,000 − 40,000 interest − 60,000 hurricane loss = **340,000**. The unusual loss stays in continuing operations, pretax.

rows.label: Discontinued operations, net of tax (enter a loss as negative)

parts.prompt: Review the draft note. For each highlighted phrase, keep it or select the correct replacement.

segments.text: The loss from hurricane damage is presented

segments.original: as an extraordinary item, net of tax
options: as an extraordinary item, net of tax
as a separate line within income from continuing operations, before tax
segments.answer: as a separate line within income from continuing operations, before tax
segments.explanation: Extraordinary items were eliminated (ASU 2015-01). Unusual or infrequent items are separate components of continuing operations, pretax.

segments.text: . The sale of the Outdoor Division qualifies as a discontinued operation because it

segments.original: represents a strategic shift that has a major effect on operations and financial results
options: represents a strategic shift that has a major effect on operations and financial results
segments.answer: represents a strategic shift that has a major effect on operations and financial results
segments.explanation: This is the correct criterion; the original wording is right. A loss or timing alone does not make a disposal a discontinued operation.

segments.text: . Prior-year results of the Outdoor Division

options: have been reclassified to discontinued operations
have been adjusted through retained earnings
segments.answer: have been reclassified to discontinued operations
segments.explanation: Comparative periods are recast so the component appears in discontinued operations for all periods presented.

segments.text: . The unrealized gain on available-for-sale debt securities is reported

segments.explanation: Unrealized (non-credit) gains and losses on AFS debt securities go to OCI.

parts.prompt: Which excerpt (paraphrased for study) governs whether the Outdoor Division is reported as a discontinued operation?

excerpts.text: A material event that is unusual in nature or occurs infrequently is reported as a separate component of income from continuing operations or disclosed in the notes.

The disposal of a component or group of components is reported in discontinued operations if it represents a strategic shift that has, or will have, a major effect on the entity's operations and financial results.
An entity reports comprehensive income either in a single continuous statement or in two separate but consecutive statements.
A long-lived asset classified as held for sale is measured at the lower of its carrying amount or fair value less cost to sell and is not depreciated.

parts.explanation: Topic 205-20 sets the strategic-shift criterion for discontinued operations. The other excerpts address unusual items, comprehensive income presentation, and held-for-sale measurement.
